Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

from pathlib import Path
base=Path('/home/USER/runs/paper/kimi-moonshot-arc2-hpl0/stream/frozen/seen-p2/play/users/u095/system/state/workspace/programs')

def make_input(line_rows, centers, start, end):
    g=[[1]*30 for _ in range(30)]
    g[start[0]][start[1]]=2
    g[end[0]][end[1]]=2
    for r,c in zip(line_rows,centers):
        g[r]=[6]*30
        for j in range(c-1,c+2): g[r][j]=3
    return g

def transform(grid):
    g=[row[:] for row in grid]
    n=len(grid); m=len(grid[0])
    reds=[(r,c) for r in range(n) for c in range(m) if grid[r][c]==2]
    start=min(reds); end=max(reds)
    line_rows=[r for r in range(n) if len(set(grid[r]))>1 and sum(v!=1 for v in grid[r])==m]
    points=[start]
    for r in line_rows:
        specials=[c for c,v in enumerate(grid[r]) if v not in (1,grid[r][0])]
        # middle of three exceptional cells
        points.append((r,specials[len(specials)//2]))
    points.append(end)
    for (r1,c1),(r2,c2) in zip(points,points[1:]):
        # Move horizontally on the row above the target line (or on end's row),
        # then vertically to the target. First segment begins below start.
        if r1==start[0]:
            hr=r1+1
        elif r2==end[0]:
            hr=r2-1
        else:
            hr=r2-1
        for c in range(min(c1,c2),max(c1,c2)+1):
            if g[hr][c]==1: g[hr][c]=2
        for r in range(min(r1,r2),max(r1,r2)+1):
            if g[r][c2]!=6 and g[r][c2]!=4: g[r][c2]=2
    return g

    g = [row[:] for row in grid]
    n, m = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    background = grid[0][0]
    path_color = next(v for row in grid for v in row if v != background and sum(x == v for row in grid for x in row) == 2)

    line_rows = [r for r in range(n) if all(v != background for v in grid[r])]

    for r in line_rows:
        line_color = grid[r][0]
        special = [c for c, v in enumerate(grid[r]) if v != line_color]
        points.append((r, special[len(special)//2]))
    points.append(end)
    for (r1, c1), (r2, c2) in zip(points, points[1:]):
        for r in range(r1 + 1, r2):
            g[r][c1] = path_color
        for c in range(min(c1, c2), max(c1, c2) + 1):
            g[r2 - 1][c] = path_color
